A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stackelberg Reward Shaping work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original HH-RLHF/SHP experiments, GPT-4 comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds distribution-transfer, robustness, reward-model disagreement and larger-backbone results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 changes the stated SRS-CD candidate construction from selecting highest-likelihood tokens to sampling from the base policy. Threshold optimization, sigmoid shaping, Q-function training and SRS-ARGS remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this pseudocode revision reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: v2 adds HarmfulQA malicious prompts and SHP-to-HH-RLHF/HarmfulQA transfer evaluation in Section 7.2. Appendix D also introduces noisy-reward and mismatched guide/evaluator scenarios. These substantially extend the tested safety and transfer conditions beyond the retained HH-RLHF/SHP evaluations.

E2.justification: The empirical comparator families remain unchanged. Section 6.2 corrects Minmax's normalization denominator from r-r_max to r_max-r_min, a substantive correction to its documented definition. The unchanged main scores do not establish that the comparator was rerun.

E3.justification: New protocols include training on SHP and testing elsewhere, adding N(0,1) noise during reward-guided decoding while scoring with clean rewards, and separating guide and evaluation reward models. v2 also adds a 27B/600-prompt setting, disagreement measurements over 300 prompts with ten responses each, and timing over 50 prompts. Original main evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 7.2 and Appendix D add distribution-shift tests, hyperparameter transfer and perturbation checks, noisy-reward tests, cross-reward validation and preference-disagreement analysis. Appendix C.2 adds latency versus candidate-count analysis. Four safety examples replace two earlier general examples, while existing ablations and CD failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new experiments continue point-estimate reporting; Gaussian reward perturbation is a robustness condition, not an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their original scores. Figure 3 and Tables 6–11 add substantial results, including noisy Eval-1 ARGS rewards of 3.31 for SRS versus 3.14 for vanilla, and Gemma-2-27B rewards of -6.31 for SRS-ARGS versus -6.48 for Minmax-ARGS. Table 5 adds response times. These are newly reported comparisons, not gains over the corresponding v1 runs.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 weakens its universal strict-improvement inequality from > to >=. Theorems 1–3, Proposition 1 and their proofs otherwise remain unchanged, moving from Appendix D to E. New Appendix F supplies a worked five-response counterexample to assigning the entire reward boost only to the highest-utility response.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about KL-regularized alignment, optimal threshold reward shaping, efficient approximation and average win–tie rates exceeding 66%. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of sigmoid noise tolerance, a hypothesis connecting reward-model disagreement to smaller transfer gains, and the cost–quality rationale for using ten candidates. It discusses GRPO integration as unevaluated future work. Existing benign-user assumptions and CD limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a repository link for its own implementation, access information for the Gemma reward model, and hyperparameters for the 27B experiment. Existing hardware, software, Q-network training settings and prompt-dependent reward-bound implementation details are retained in Appendix G, formerly E.

R1.justification: References are added for HarmfulQA, Gemma, reward modeling, ranking disagreement, GRPO and strategic AI safety. Future Work modestly expands the incentive-design positioning. The main related-work distinctions remain; bibliographic and preprint-to-publication updates do not constitute separate research additions.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory and pseudocode revisions, edits the title and author-credit wording, and adds Future Work and an appendix contents list. The main argument order and most retained prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts two-column main text and extensively reflows the displays. It replaces the original game schematic with a workflow diagram, adds shaping and transfer figures, introduces Tables 6–11, expands Table 5 with timing, and revises the qualitative figure selection. Existing appendix plots are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Transfer, noisy-reward, independent-reward and 27B tests usefully extend v1's benchmark and GPT-4 evidence. Formula and corollary corrections, explanatory figures and the implementation link also improve precision and reproducibility. The gains remain limited by point-estimate-only validation, inconsistent Eval-2 CD baseline values in Table 7 (3.10 versus 3.16), and the unexplained candidate-selection revision alongside unchanged main results.
